Burst engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Burst rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app rapid still capture from product-page copy:

  • Camera Burst mode — Apple Camera feature that captures a rapid sequence of still photos while the user holds the shutter button or uses a volume or Burst gesture. Labeled 连拍, 连拍模式, or 连拍照片 in zh-Hans system UI. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • Rapid still buffering & frame capture — capture logic that records many still frames per second over a brief window, then lets the buyer pick the sharpest frame. Your listing may mention Burst photos or high-speed still sequence; building burst pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Frame selection & best-frame picker — post-capture UI that shows a filmstrip of burst stills so buyers choose the best sports, kids, or pet frame. Listing copy explains those buyer benefits; burst sample still production is outside AppLocale scope.
  • AVFoundation & capture sessions — camera session code configured for rapid still capture with storage and thermal management. Entitlements and capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Burst value to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Burst support in the binary.

A working Burst story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Burst vs Slo-Mo vs Time-Lapse vs Live Photos vs Cinematic Mode vs Action Mode vs Panorama — do not conflate

US/EU indie teams often merge ten Camera string families. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets Burst — a rapid sequence of still photos while holding the shutter — not slow-motion video, not sped-up long recording, not motion stills, not cinematic video blur, not video stabilization, not wide stitches, and not other single-shot still modes:

  • Burst & rapid still capture (this page) — paragraphs and frame text explaining "Burst", "Burst Mode", "Burst photos", "Rapid stills", "High-speed still sequence", "Hold shutter", "Pick the best frame", 连拍, 连拍模式, 连拍照片, 连拍相机. Many still frames captured in quick succession — pick the sharpest later.
  • Slo-Mo listing copy (different) — high-frame-rate slow playback of a short captured video moment: Slo-Mo, Slow Motion, 慢动作, 慢动作拍摄, 慢动作视频. A short moment recorded at high fps, then played back slowly — video, not rapid still bursts. Covered on our Slo-Mo guide.
  • Time-Lapse listing copy (different) — long-duration recording compressed into a short sped-up video: Time-Lapse, 延时拍摄, 延时摄影, 延时视频. Speeds long recording up — not fires rapid stills. Covered on our Time-Lapse guide.
  • Live Photos listing copy (different) — still photos with a few seconds of motion before and after the shutter: Live Photos, 实况照片, 动态照片. One still plus a short motion clip at normal speed — not dozens of burst stills. Covered on our Live Photos guide.
  • Cinematic Mode listing copy (different) — shallow-depth cinematic video look with focus transitions: Cinematic Mode, 浅景深电影效果视频, 电影效果模式. Depth-of-field video storytelling — not burst still capture. Covered on our Cinematic Mode guide.
  • Action Mode listing copy (different) — extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage: Action Mode, 动作模式, 运动防抖. Video stabilization — not rapid still burst marketing. Covered on our Action Mode guide.
  • Panorama listing copy (different) — wide horizontal or vertical stitched still photos while panning the phone: Panorama, 全景, 全景模式. Ultra-wide still stitches — not rapid burst sequences. Covered on our Panorama guide.
  • Night Mode listing copy (different) — low-light capture with longer exposure and computational blending: Night Mode, 夜间模式, 夜景模式. Low-light still photography — not sports or pet burst demos unless your English listing shows Night Mode burst specifically. Covered on our Night Mode guide.
  • Portrait Mode listing copy (different) — shallow depth-of-field still photography with soft background blur: Portrait Mode, 人像模式, 景深虚化. Subject-background separation on stills — not burst sequence marketing. Covered on our Portrait Mode guide.
  • Macro listing copy (different) — extreme close-up still photography at minimum focus distance: Macro, 微距, 微距近拍. Close-up detail shots — not rapid action burst stills. Covered on our Macro guide.
  • Photographic Styles listing copy (different) — still-photo tone presets at capture: Photographic Styles, 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Photo color grading — not burst capture. Covered on our Photographic Styles guide.

Burst fires many stills in rapid succession so you pick the best frame. Slo-Mo stretches a short video moment into slow playback. Time-Lapse compresses hours into seconds of video. Live Photos adds motion around a single still shutter moment. Cinematic Mode adds cinematic depth-of-field to video. Action Mode stabilizes handheld walking-running video. Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Night Mode brightens low-light shots. Portrait Mode blurs backgrounds on stills. Macro captures extreme close-ups. Photographic Styles adjusts tone at capture. Mixing vocabulary across those surfaces on one product page reads like confused localization — scope each screenshot frame to the workflow it actually shows.

Burst-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Rapid still-capture listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Burst feature — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Burst phrasing

US pages use "Burst", "Burst Mode", "Burst photos", "Rapid stills", "High-speed still sequence", "Hold shutter", or "Pick the best frame." Apple's Simplified Chinese Camera vocabulary often uses 连拍 for the general burst label, 连拍模式 for capture-mode marketing, 连拍照片 for the rapid still output, and 连拍相机 when burst is the hero camera feature. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing burst capabilities your app does not support.

Hold shutter vs volume burst vs gesture

Burst marketing often shows distinct triggers — on-screen shutter hold, volume-button burst, or swipe-to-burst gesture. Chinese buyers expect per-frame captions: 长按快门 for hold shutter, 连拍模式 for the mode toggle, 音量键连拍 for volume-button burst — not one generic "强大相机" string on every frame.

Use-case-specific demos

Sports action, kids mid-jump, pets in motion, and splash impact each signal different buyer intent. zh-Hans overlays should name the scenario the frame shows: 运动连拍 for sports burst, 儿童连拍 for kids burst, 宠物连拍 for pet burst, 水花连拍 for splash burst — not English "Sports burst" pasted through machine translation without context.

Filmstrip and best-frame picker

When your English listing markets frame selection after a burst, zh-Hans overlays may use 连拍照片 for the capture output and 挑选最佳照片 for the picker UI — distinct steps with different screenshot vocabulary on the same product page.

Do not conflate with Slo-Mo, Time-Lapse, or Live Photos

Burst captures many stills in rapid succession. Slo-Mo slows a short high-fps video moment down. Time-Lapse speeds long recording up into a short clip. Live Photos adds a few seconds of motion around one still shutter moment. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately — 慢动作 belongs on Slo-Mo frames, 延时拍摄 belongs on Time-Lapse frames, 实况照片 belongs on Live Photos frames, 连拍 belongs on Burst frames.

Do not conflate with Cinematic Mode, Panorama, or Action Mode

Burst fires rapid still frames while you hold the shutter. Cinematic Mode adds shallow-depth cinematic look to video. Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Action Mode stabilizes handheld walking-running video. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need burst search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 连拍, 连拍模式, and 连拍照片 each signal different intent from Slo-Mo 慢动作 keywords or Panorama 全景 keywords.

What good zh-Hans Burst listing copy looks like

Burst-centric listings name the hold-shutter rapid-still workflow in plain zh-Hans — not a word-for-word mirror of English brochure lines:

  • Subtitle — one clause on burst or rapid still-capture outcome; room for 连拍 or 连拍模式 within 30 characters — e.g. "连拍模式，定格瞬间" or "连拍照片，挑选最佳"
  • Keywords — mix 连拍, 连拍模式, 连拍照片, 连拍相机, and category nouns (摄影, 相机); avoid English-only "Burst" stuffing — see Simplified Chinese keywords
  • Description — lead with the hold-shutter-and-capture-many-stills workflow; mention sports, kids, or pet use cases only when your app actually supports those scenarios or equivalent burst paths
  • Screenshot overlays — short lines naming what the frame shows: 连拍, 连拍模式, 挑选最佳照片 — not "Burst" pasted through machine translation
  • Voice match — same 你/您 and punctuation habits as your other zh-Hans fields
  • Honest scope — if your app supports standard Camera burst only but not custom frame-rate burst controls, zh-Hans copy should not imply pro sports burst unless your English listing already claims it accurately

zh-Hans Burst captions can differ idiomatically from en-US overlays when the on-screen feature is the same — avoid mirroring comma-heavy English marketing onto iPhone art.

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines — rewritten from your English Burst marketing originals.

Can AppLocale implement Burst capture or rapid still buffering?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. Burst capture engineering, frame-buffer wiring, and burst sample still design are outside AppLocale scope.

How is this different from Slo-Mo, Time-Lapse, Live Photos, Cinematic Mode, Action Mode, Panorama, Night Mode, Portrait Mode, Macro, or Photographic Styles?

Burst copy markets rapid still capture in quick succession while holding the shutter — 连拍, 连拍模式, 连拍照片. Slo-Mo copy markets high-fps slow playback of a short video moment — 慢动作, 慢动作拍摄, 慢动作视频. Time-Lapse copy markets long-duration recording compressed into a short sped-up video — 延时拍摄, 延时摄影, 延时视频. Live Photos copy markets one still plus a few seconds of motion — 实况照片. Cinematic Mode copy markets shallow-depth cinematic video — 浅景深电影效果视频. Action Mode copy markets handheld video stabilization — 动作模式, 运动防抖. Panorama copy markets wide stitched stills — 全景, 全景模式. Night Mode copy markets low-light capture — 夜间模式. Portrait Mode copy markets background blur on stills — 人像模式, 景深虚化. Macro copy markets extreme close-ups — 微距, 微距近拍. Photographic Styles copy markets still-photo tone presets — 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Each surface has separate screenshot vocabulary.
